assignment: Independent source-quality review of PayrollRules.CalculateLateDeduction(Money,int,int,int,int,double), focusing on settings validation, arithmetic and rounding, ledger effects, payroll consumption, and existing test source. Static only; tests not executed.

receipt.author: financial_integrity
receipt.reasoning_summary: Combines integer-truncated normal hourly rate and penalty hours, multiplies by double multiplier, rounds ToEven and casts to long. Does not validate non-finite/extreme multiplier. Because evaluation is left-associative, rate.Piastres*hours is a long intermediate before multiplication by double, with possible unchecked overflow. Returns components; caller posts.

calculation_and_edges.expression: rate = NormalHourlyRate(dailyWage, workdayHours); hours = CalculateLatePenaltyHours(lateMinutes, graceMinutes, maxPenaltyHours); amount = Money.FromPiastres((long)Math.Round(rate.Piastres * hours * latePenaltyMultiplier))
calculation_and_edges.units: rate is piastres per scheduled work hour; hours is a discrete penalty-hour count; multiplier is a double factor; amount is rounded integer piastres.
rounding_and_overflow: The default Math.Round overload uses midpoint-to-even rounding.

rate.Piastres and hours are long/int, so their leftmost product is evaluated in long arithmetic before multiplication by the double multiplier. Very large rate/hour products can overflow the long intermediate depending on checked context; project/runtime execution was not inspected or tested for this case.
The final Math.Round result is cast to long without an explicit range check. Non-finite/extreme multiplier behavior is not validated here and no runtime outcome is claimed.
The hourly rate itself is integer division in NormalHourlyRate, so wage not divisible by workday hours loses remainder before penalty multiplication; nonpositive workdayHours returns a zero rate.
calculation_and_edges.settings_boundary: SettingsQueryService defaults are grace=15, maxPenaltyHours=2, LatePenaltyMultiplier=2.0. UpdateSettingsHandler requires settings_manage for these fields but directly assigns LateGraceMinutes, MaxLatePenaltyHours and LatePenaltyMultiplier when supplied, without visible numeric range checks. See prior reviewer-owned handoff financial-payroll-settings-validation-correction-delta-review-2026-10-24.json; no owner policy was found defining allowed bounds.

callers_and_settlement_effect.effect: Calls CalculateLateDeduction only when lateMinutes>grace and employee daily wage is positive. Posts an employee-ledger Deduction debit only when Amount.IsPositive, keyed by employee/date; negative or zero amount is suppressed in this automatic path.

Under an employee-ledger lock and transaction, loads settings, computes old/new amounts, then posts Adjustment debit when new-old is positive or Adjustment credit when negative. With ordinary positive settings, reducing a penalty creates a credit. If maxPenaltyHours or multiplier is negative, a positive penalty-hour case can produce a negative amount; increasing recorded lateness can then create a credit rather than a debit. This is a source-arithmetic consequence conditional on malformed settings, not proof such settings are used or forbidden.
Loads monthly employee ledger facts and calls CalculatePayrollLines; it does not call this helper directly.

Includes Debit amounts for LedgerEntryType Deduction or Adjustment in deductions, but does not include Adjustment credits in base/overtime/extra-shift/bonus totals. Thus a correction credit is not reflected as an earning in the payroll line. This cross-references existing FIN012/Adjustment-credit omission; it is not a new finding from this review.

tests_reviewed_static_only.coverage: Tests grace/no-penalty and ordinary late deduction under positive defaults. The pure hour-rule tests cover grace and minute 60/61. No negative max/multiplier, non-finite/extreme multiplier, integer-rate remainder, long-intermediate overflow or correction sign case.

Inspected late check-in integration case is immediate/no-penalty; it does not prove positive automatic deduction posting or malformed settings. Correction cases at lines 267-284 and 244-284 exercise state/correction, not the requested negative-setting sign outcome.
Tests ordinary payroll net from daily wage/overtime/other ledger facts; no late-penalty configuration or correction-credit-to-payroll assertion.

counterevidence_and_limits: Defaults are positive and ordinary (grace 15/max 2/multiplier 2.0); no bad persisted setting or financial incident was inspected.
Biometric check-in suppresses negative computed amount, so malformed negative values do not cause an automatic credit through that specific writer.

Correction requires attendance_manage plus manager approval, uses a transaction and idempotent request/audit workflow. This protects the correction operation but does not define valid payroll settings.
Policy is absent from reviewed code/tests: cannot conclude negative max/multiplier or unusually high grace are forbidden, nor confirm a product defect without owner decision.
A correction credit's omission from payroll line income overlaps the existing FIN012 concern; do not duplicate it here.
verdict: The receipt's core calculation description is corroborated and this function is financially material through automatic deductions and correction adjustments. Source confirms conditional sign changes under negative settings and a long intermediate before double multiplication. No new finding recommended until payroll policy defines permitted ranges; overflow/runtime behavior remains unverified.
recommended_followup: Cross-reference FIN012 for Adjustment credits. Ask payroll policy owner to define nonnegative/max/grace/multiplier bounds; if negative values are out of policy, enforce at settings boundary and add source-level tests for negative settings and correction debit/credit direction, alongside overflow/midpoint/rate-remainder cases.
